name: Jehoram
bio:
Jehoram, son of Ahab, became king of Israel in his brother Ahaziah's place, since Ahaziah died without a son — in the second year of the other Jehoram, son of Jehoshaphat, who was then reigning in Judah (2 Kings 1:17).

## 📖 Core Story: War Against Moab

Jehoram did evil in the LORD's eyes, though not as badly as his father and mother, since he put away the image of Baal that Ahab had made; he still clung to the sins of Jeroboam (2 Kings 3:1-3). When Mesha, king of Moab, rebelled after Ahab's death, Jehoram mustered all Israel and persuaded Jehoshaphat of Judah and the king of Edom to join his campaign. The allied armies nearly perished of thirst in the wilderness of Edom until Elisha, consulted at Jehoshaphat's insistence, prophesied water and victory. The campaign succeeded: Moab was routed and devastated, though Mesha's horrifying sacrifice of his own son at Kir Hareseth caused the allied kings to abandon the siege and go home (2 Kings 3:4-27).

## 📖 Core Story: Elisha's Warnings, and the Famine of Samaria

During renewed war with Syria, Elisha repeatedly warned Jehoram of Ben-Hadad's ambush plans, saving him again and again, until Ben-Hadad sent an army to seize Elisha at Dothan — an attempt Elisha foiled by blinding the soldiers and leading them into Samaria, where Jehoram, at Elisha's insistence, fed them and sent them home instead of killing them (2 Kings 6:8-23). When Ben-Hadad later besieged Samaria outright, the resulting famine grew so severe that people resorted to eating their own children; Jehoram, hearing of it, tore his clothes in horror and, blaming Elisha for the disaster, swore to have him beheaded (2 Kings 6:24-33).

## 📖 Core Story: The Famine Broken

Elisha prophesied the famine would end within a day, and it did: the Syrian army fled their own camp in panic after the LORD made them hear phantom armies approaching, and four desperate lepers discovered the abandoned camp and reported it. Jehoram, suspecting a trap, sent scouts who confirmed the Syrians were truly gone, and the starving city plundered the camp, fulfilling Elisha's prophecy of cheap grain at the gate exactly as foretold (2 Kings 7:1-20).

## 📖 Core Story: Wounded at Ramoth Gilead

After Hazael murdered Ben-Hadad and seized the throne of Syria, Jehoram joined Ahaziah, king of Judah, in battle against Hazael at Ramoth Gilead, where the Syrians wounded him. He withdrew to Jezreel to recover, and Ahaziah went down to visit him there (2 Kings 8:28-29).
